front.title: CCN NETRJS server messages to remote user

section.name: A. INITIAL CONNECTION, SIGNON, AND SIGNOFF

li.t: If CCN refuses an ICP to a NETRJS socket, it means either that there is no free core within the NCP region, or that CCN's software is crashing.
Once ICP is completed, CCN might send the user one of the following messages and close the Telnet connections:
li.artwork: NRJ110I NETRJS PORTS BUSY. TRY LATER
li.t: This may be expected occasionally; frequent occurrance should be reported to CCN User Relations (825-7548), or to BELL@CCN.
li.artwork: NRJ111I RJS NOT UP, TRY LATER

li.t: Normally, however, the user will receive a READY message:
li.artwork: NRJ876R CCN NETRJS READY. ENTER SIGNON
li.t: If the user sends no operator input for 3 minutes, CCN will send:
li.artwork:
NRJ308R SIGNON TIMEOUT EXCEEDED
NRJ205R NETRJS SESSION TERMINATED
li.t: and close the Telnet connection. If he sends an invalid SIGNON command, he will receive the message:
Finally, a valid signon will be acknowledged by RJS with the message:
li.artwork: RJS750I TERMINAL -termid- HAS SIGNED ONTO RJS

li.t: If the user terminates the session by entering a SIGNOFF command, NETRJS will wait until all data transfer has completed before sending the message:
and closing the Telnet connection.

section.name: B. REMOTE SITE OR NETWORK FAILURES

li.t: During data transfer, the user must be reasonably responsive. If not, CCN will close the data transfer connection and send the remote operator message:
li.artwork: NRJ504I DATA TRANSFER TIMEOUT FOR THE -device-, -termid-

li.t: if -device- is PRINTER or PUNCH, user site stopped accepting bits (sending "allocates") for over 5 minutes.
if -device- is READER, user site left reader connection open without sending any bits for 5 minutes.

During data transfer on the CR connection, CCN may detect an incorrect header or record, presumably due to user site software or Network transmission error. The following messages beginning with the word "BAD" will follow an NRJ512I message containing the faulty header in hex:
li.artwork: NRJ505I BAD HEADER SEQUENCE FOR NETRJS READER
li.t: Sequence number in transaction header does not match internal counter of records passed.
li.artwork: NRJ506I BAD HEADER LENGTH FOR NETRJS READER
li.t: Length given in header exceeds 880 bytes.
li.artwork: NRJ507I BAD HEADER TYPE FOR NETRJS READER
li.t: Type code in header is not X'FF' (data) or X'FE' (end-of-data)
li.artwork: NRJ511I BAD FILL BIT COUNT FOR NETRJS READER
li.t: The filler bit count in header is not a multiple of 8.
If the header is correct but a data record is faulty, the following message will be sent to a remote user:
A protocol error was detected in the READER stream. CCN will close the stream and ready it to be reopened so the remote user may retry the data transfer operation. The valid -code- values are:

tr.td: Device id byte has high bit off.
End of transaction in the middle of a data line.
Truncated input line longer than 255 bytes.
In compressed text, string control byte has high bit off.
In compressed text, duplicate blank string extends line longer than 255 bytes.
In compressed text, duplicate character string extends line longer than 255 bytes.
In compressed text, character string extends line longer than 255 bytes.

li.t: Finally, if the user aborts his data transfer, he receives the message:
li.artwork: NRJ502I NETRJS -device- DATA TRANSFER ABORTED BY USER -termid-.

section.name: C. CCN FAILURES

li.t: The CCN operator can cancel a NETRJS session, aborting any open data transfer streams and sending the message:
li.artwork: NRJ204I NETRJS SESSION ABORTED BY CENTRAL OPERATOR, TERM= -termid-

li.t: Any of the following messages indicate a serious CCN Network software problem, and will cause the session to be aborted:
li.artwork:
NRJ106A NETRJS DEAD - EXCHANGE INOPERATIVE
NRJ201A NETRJS DT SOCKET ERROR - BAD LISTEN
NRJ208A NETRJS PROGRAM CHECK IN -device-, code=ccc
NRJ209A NETRJS LOAD FAILED FOR -device-, code=xx
NRJ304I RJS LINE HANDLER DEAD
NRJ401I RJS LINE HANDLER DEAD
NRJ402I RJS LINE HANDLER DEAD
li.t: Any of these should be reported to CCN.

Besides global catastrophes like these above, the user might encounter a failure of a particular data transfer process. These do not terminate the session, only cause the data connection to be refused or terminated; the user can try again to open the data connection. Repeated failure should be reported to CCN.
li.artwork:
NRJ501I NO CORE FOR DATA TRANSFER BUFFER -device-
NRJ503I NO CORE FOR DATA TRANSFER WORKAREA -device-
NRJ207I NO CORE FOR-device-DATA TRANSFER MODULE
li.t: Due to core memory limitations in CCN's NCP, -device- cannot be started now. The data transfer connection indicated by -device- will be refused. This may happen occasionally during active periods, but repeated occurrences should be reported to CCN.
li.artwork:
NRJ509I -device- DATA TRANSFER DEAD
NRJ510I -device- DATA TRANSFER DEAD
NRJ602I line STREAM ERROR - PRINTER, -code-
NRJ602I line STREAM ERROR - PUNCH, -code-
li.t: CCN data transfer failed, but recovery may be possible. User may try again.
